title: Adding noise to a sandbagging model can reveal its true capabilities
primary_claim: Adding noise to the weights of a sandbagging Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct model can increase its GSM8k performance (revealing hidden capability), replicating the main effect from 'Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models' with a different model and dataset.
quote: If you add noise to the parameters of a model that is sandbagging, then sometimes its performance on a task can increase.
metric: accuracy on 350 GSM8k questions vs weight noise level
target_value: for some seeds, accuracy of the sandbagging-prompted model increases as noise is added, while the normal-prompted model's accuracy decreases with noise
tolerance_rationale: headline is not a single scalar; judge by hand

needed: gsm8k (main config), first 350 rows of the train split

inspector_notes: Small, simple ARENA-capstone-style repo with no pinned versions but a very direct, single-file entrypoint; requirements.txt lists transformer-lens but the actual final experiment (exp07) uses plain HF transformers, per the README's own note about switching backends mid-project. Committed logs/ CSVs from the original run are included, so the qualitative claim can be checked without even re-running anything.
headline_artifact: logs/20250529_qwen_prompts1/*.csv (per noise_scale/seed accuracy on GSM8K, sandbag vs original prompt) -- committed logs already show the qualitative effect (some seeds: sandbag accuracy rises with noise while original accuracy falls)

extension.what_varies: 20 additional noise seeds (10-29) at noise 0.001 and 0.002, sandbag prompt only; model, code, prompts, data, decoding, env (.venv_tf453 = bit-identical to parent) unchanged
extension.rationale: R-3 left the author-vs-parent discrepancy (author 6/10 seeds, ours 9/10) unexplained by transformers or torch; test whether both are draws from one collapse-rate distribution.
